name: Barbastro – Claretian Martyrs Museum
story: Barbastro stayed in Republican hands after the rising. In the first weeks of the war anarchist militias carried out one of the worst killings of clergy in the Republican zone here. The dead included 51 Claretian missionaries, mostly young seminarians, as well as Benedictines, Piarists, cathedral canons and diocesan priests. Bishop Florentino Asensio was also killed. The diocese lost a larger share of its clergy than any other in Spain. The 51 Claretians were beatified in 1992. A museum in the Claretian house tells their story.
see: The museum in the Claretian community's house, with the seminarians' letters and belongings and a crypt with their remains.
plan: Museo de los Mártires Claretianos, C/ Conde 4, Barbastro, about 50 km east of Huesca. Usually open Tuesday–Saturday 10:00–13:00 and 17:00–19:00 and Sunday 17:00–19:00; hours change, so check with the museum or the Barbastro tourist office before you go.
